newsitem.title: USA: MCI cuts long distance rates, matches AT&T.
newsitem.headline: MCI cuts long distance rates, matches AT&T.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp, moving to match rate cuts announced earlier by AT&T Corp, said Monday it will cut its basic long distance calling rates by five percent for daytime and evening calls and by 15 percent for nighttime and weekend calls.
MCI's announcement of its cuts came just hours after AT&T said it would cut its basic service rates by the same rate.
"We've promised we would pass savings on, and now we've delivered," said MCI spokeswoman Sheila Blackwell.

Both AT&T and MCI are cutting rates in response to a May 7 order by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission that local telephone companies reduce the access fees they levy on long distance providers for initiating and completing long distance calls.

The savings to the long distance companies are estimated at about $1.7 billion, although MCI and AT&T both complain that regional Bell companies have implemented only $1.5 billion in reductions so far.

MCI is filing its rate change tariff with the FCC on Tuesday and the new rate will take effect Wednesday, Blackwell said. The cut in the base rate should benefit MCI discount subscribers whose plans base their discounts on the company's basic rate, she said.
AT&T's rate cut -- which will affect subscribers to its basic long distance plan, not discount plan members for now -- will become effective July 15, it said.
Sprint Corp officials said Monday they have not determined what amount of reductions are attributable to Sprint and therefore have not formulated a rate reduction plan.
MCI shares slipped 31/32 to 38-9/16 on the Nasdaq. AT&T shares lost 11/16 to 35-1/16.
